subproblem.title: The anchor member and the infinite-mass members of 𝓜 (properties (6), (7); conditional on (IM), (MON), (MB))
subproblem.statement: Assume (IM) — the frozen type of the grandparent's registered dependency im_mass_measure, which is the selected node's first leading hypothesis: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every IMRep R of T in U: (a) M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ U; (b) for x ∈ U, x ∈ spt T if and only if R.measure(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0; (c) R′.measure = R.measure for every IMRep R′ of T in U. Assume (MON) — the frozen type of the grandparent's registered dependency monotonicity (the selected node's second leading hypothesis): for all P, n, d ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ n ≤ d ≤ P, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold N with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ and every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0: (i) for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ ≥ 0 such that ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) is monotone on (0, R) whenever B̄_R(y) ⊆ K; (ii) if N = ℝ^P, then ρ ↦ ofReal(1/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) is monotone on (0, R) whenever B_R(y) ⊆ U; (iii) there is Θ, upper semicontinuous on U, with HasMassDensity T y (Θ y) for all y ∈ U; (iv) every density of T at a point of spt T is ≥ 1. Assume (MB) — the frozen type of the grandparent's registered dependency moving_blowups (the selected node's third leading hypothesis): for all n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k, U, N ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with 1 ≤ n, U open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold, (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, T minimizing in U ∩ N, spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U, and for all x ∈ U, x_j → x and λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0, there are a strictly increasing φ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}) such that blowUp T x_{φ(j)} λ_{φ(j)} ⇀ C in ℝ^{n+k} (ConvergesWeakly), MassMeasuresConverge holds for the same sequence, C is minimizing in ℝ^{n+k} and ∂C = 0. Let n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k and 1 ≤ n, let U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} be open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U. Let z ∈ ℝ^{n+k} and r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(z) ⊆ U, and let RT be an IMRep of T in U; write μ_T := RT.measure, W := B_{2r}(z) and η_{a,t} := dilation a t (η_{a,t}(v) = t⁻¹(v − a)). Let 𝓜 be a set of measures on ℝ^{n+k} such that μ ∈ 𝓜 if and only if either (PS) μ = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) • (μ_T⌞W).map η_{a,t} for some a ∈ ℝ^{n+k} and some t with 0 < t ≤ r and dist(a, z) ≤ r − t; or (ZS) μ = RS.measure for some S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}) and some IMRep RS of S in ℝ^{n+k} for which there are points c_i, scales t_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) and a point b with dist(c_i, z) < r − t_i for every i, t_i → 0, c_i → b, and blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S in ℝ^{n+k} (ConvergesWeakly). (These are the selected node's positive-scale members μ_{x,λ} and zero-scale members, with (a, t) = (z + rx, rλ), c_i = z + rx_i, t_i = rλ_i, b = z + rx̄.) Let dens be a function of a measure and a point with dens μ x = (limsup_{ρ→0⁺} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ))).toReal for all μ, x (limsup in [0, ∞] along 𝓝[>]0, ω_n = unitBallVolume n). Then (6) there is μ₀ ∈ 𝓜 such that dens μ₀ w = θ whenever ‖w‖ < 1 and HasMassDensity T (z + r•w) θ; and (7) for every ν ∈ 𝓜 with ν(ℝ^{n+k}) = ∞ there are S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}), points x_i ∈ B_r(z) and scales λ_i > 0 with λ_i → 0 such that blowUp T x_i λ_i ⇀ S in ℝ^{n+k} (ConvergesWeakly), S is minimizing in ℝ^{n+k}, ∂S = 0, and HasMassDensity S y (dens ν y) for every y ∈ ℝ^{n+k}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 8 and 9 of the selected node's supplied proof (anchor member; infinite-mass members, parent 2(f), 2(b)) with its (0j); Simon 7.3.3, proof of (1): T itself appears in 𝒯 as η_{0,1#}T′ and the members with λ = 0 are minimizing in all of ℝ^{n+ℓ} (chapter-07.txt lines 443–465). Positive-scale members are written (a, t) = (z + rx, rλ). Siblings used: zero_limit_minimizing (Submission.dimred_tr_bc_zero_limit_minimizing, with (MB)) and ambient_calculus (Submission.idtp_fons_cc_ambient_calculus) parts (1), (2), (3).
Notation: μ_T := RT.measure, W := B_{2r}(z), ω_n := unitBallVolume n, q(m, x, ρ) := m(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) ∈ [0, ∞]. ω_n is the volume of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ, hence 0 < ω_n < ∞.
1. (Finite total mass of positive-scale members.) For admissible (a, t), (ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) • (μ_T⌞W).map(dilation a t))(univ) = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ)·μ_T(W) (ambient_calculus (2); the preimage of univ is univ) < ∞, because μ_T(W) ≤ μ_T(B̄_{2r}(z)) = ∫⁻_{RT.carrier ∩ B̄_{2r}(z)} RT.mult dHⁿ < ∞ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact B̄_{2r}(z) ⊆ U).
2. (Property (6).) Let μ₀ := ofReal(r⁻¹ⁿ) • (μ_T⌞W).map(dilation z r). It is (PS) with (a, t) := (z, r) (0 < r ≤ r and dist(z, z) = 0 ≤ r − r), so μ₀ ∈ 𝓜. Let ‖w‖ < 1 and HasMassDensity T (z + r•w) θ, i.e. θ ≥ 0 and q′(ρ) := M_{B_ρ(z+r•w)}(T)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) → ofReal θ as ρ → 0⁺.
 (a) For 0 < ρ < 1 − ‖w‖: B_{rρ}(z + r•w) ⊆ W ⊆ U (dist(v, z) < rρ + r‖w‖ < r). By ambient_calculus (2) and (3), μ₀(B_ρ(w)) = ofReal(r⁻¹ⁿ)·(μ_T⌞W)(B_{rρ}(z + r•w)) = ofReal(r⁻¹ⁿ)·μ_T(B_{rρ}(z + r•w)) = ofReal(r⁻¹ⁿ)·M_{B_{rρ}(z+r•w)}(T) ((IM)(a) for T).
 (b) Since ofReal(r⁻¹ⁿ) = ofReal(rⁿ)⁻¹ and ofReal((rρ)ⁿ) = ofReal(rⁿ)·ofReal(ρⁿ), with ofReal(rⁿ) and ω_n in (0, ∞), (a) gives q(μ₀, w, ρ) = q′(rρ) for 0 < ρ < 1 − ‖w‖ (ENNReal.div_eq_inv_mul, ENNReal.mul_inv).
 (c) ρ ↦ rρ tends to 0 within (0, ∞) as ρ → 0⁺ (continuous, positive for ρ > 0), so q′(rρ) → ofReal θ (Tendsto.comp). By (b), q(μ₀, w, ·) agrees with ρ ↦ q′(rρ) on (0, 1 − ‖w‖), a neighbourhood of 0 in 𝓝[>]0, so q(μ₀, w, ρ) → ofReal θ (Tendsto.congr').
 (d) Hence limsup_{ρ→0⁺} q(μ₀, w, ρ) = ofReal θ (Filter.Tendsto.limsup_eq; 𝓝[>]0 is nontrivial), and by the defining equation dens μ₀ w = (ofReal θ).toReal = θ (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, θ ≥ 0).
3. (Property (7).) Let ν ∈ 𝓜 with ν(univ) = ∞. By step 1, ν is not (PS); so ν = RS.measure for an IMRep RS of some S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{n+k}) with zero-scale data (c_i, t_i, hts, b).
 (a) Put xs := (c_i), lams := (t_i) and hlams := hts. Then xs_i ∈ B_r(z), since dist(c_i, z) < r − t_i < r; lams → 0; and blowUp T xs_i lams_i ⇀ S is part of the data.
 (b) dist(b, z) ≤ r (limit of dist(c_i, z) < r), so b ∈ B̄_r(z) ⊆ U, and zero_limit_minimizing (with (MB), the hypotheses of T and x := b) gives IsMinimizingIn S univ and BoundaryVanishes S.
 (c) Apply (MON) to S with P := n + k, d := n + k and U = N = univ (ambient_calculus (1); (closure univ ∖ univ) ∩ univ = ∅; S minimizing in univ ∩ univ = univ; spt S ⊆ univ ∩ univ; ∂S = 0). Part (iii) gives Θ with HasMassDensity S y (Θ y) for every y ∈ univ.
 (d) Fix y. By (IM)(a) for S (univ open, RS represents S), M_{B_ρ(y)}(S) = RS.measure(B_ρ(y)) = ν(B_ρ(y)) for every ρ. So HasMassDensity S y (Θ y) says Θ y ≥ 0 and q(ν, y, ρ) → ofReal(Θ y) as ρ → 0⁺. As in 2(d), dens ν y = (ofReal(Θ y)).toReal = Θ y. Hence HasMassDensity S y (dens ν y).
 (e) S, xs, lams and hlams satisfy all requirements of (7). ∎
proof_key_steps: Positive-scale members have finite total mass ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ)·μ_T(B_{2r}(z)), so an infinite-mass member is a zero-scale member.
Anchor μ₀ = (μ_T⌞B_{2r}(z))^{z,r}: its density ratio at w is the density ratio of T at z + rw at radius rρ, so dens μ₀ w = θ.

An infinite-mass member is the weight of an admissible zero-scale limit S (centres in B_r(z)); S is minimizing with ∂S = 0 (zero_limit_minimizing), and (MON)(iii) with (IM)(a) gives HasMassDensity S y (dens ν y).

audit.reason: The anchor follows from the exact scaled density ratio and nonnegative density. Finite total mass excludes positive-scale infinite members; zero-scale data, MB, MON and IM establish every clause of property (7).
